rows.description: Flickering diya, incense, chanting or a gurudwara or church hush hold a toddler's gaze with wonder. Caregivers let the child watch and take part gently, whatever the faith at home.

rows.description: Sitting on a grandmother's lap during aarti or bedtime prayer, the child feels loved and part of the family. Rituals shared with warmth become safe memories, not obligation.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: awe, worship

rows.description: A feverish or hurt child wants to be held and will not be put down. Comfort, water, rest and a steady voice are right; call a doctor for high fever or worrying signs, and never scold clinginess.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, fear
related mind states: anxiety, hurt

rows.description: White coats, injections and strange rooms frighten a toddler, who cries and resists. Parents stay close, hold the child, tell the truth simply (a small pinch), and never threaten the doctor as punishment.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, dependence
related mind states: fear

rows.description: A kiss on the scrape and a hug after a fall tell the child her pain matters. Acknowledging the hurt first and calmly, without saying it is nothing, teaches trust and later resilience.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: dependence, fear
related mind states: affection, calm, trust, hurt

rows.description: When adults shout or fight, the child freezes, covers ears, cries or clings, feeling the danger she cannot understand. Adults should lower voices, move the quarrel away, and reassure her afterwards.
graph_context: related mind states: anger, fear

rows.description: Being shouted at or seeing violence overwhelms a toddler, who may blame herself in feeling. Caregivers must stop it, repair with a calm hug, and seek help if anger at home is frequent.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear
related mind states: affection, anger, calm, overwhelm

rows.description: Told no to a wanted thing, the toddler screams or drops to the floor: rage with no words yet. Hold the limit gently, name the feeling, let the storm pass, and offer a safe alternative.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance

rows.description: After many calm, consistent limits, the toddler sometimes hears no, sighs and moves on. Consistency from every adult builds this. Praise it quietly and do not expect it every time.
